subject: QBR prep — slot/runbook review: GPU cost & utilization levers
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena@cloudops.io>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QBR prep — slot/runbook review: GPU cost & utilization levers

Team,

As we pull together the QBR briefing for the Executive Review (Aug 18), we need one consolidated runbook that explains how we will hold runway while hitting product performance targets. The immediate focus: GPU spend profile, utilization uplift opportunities, and experiments we can run now that will materially move unit economics by the next quarter.

Attached: infra-qbr-runbook-v1.pdf (draft runbook) and qbr-slot-planning.xlsx (capacity sheet). Please review the runbook and add comments to the Drive doc. High-level asks: 

- Markus / Aditya: populate the "short list" of levers with rough delta-to-unit-cost (percent) and rough timeline (1W, 2–4W, 8+W). Prioritize levers that are non-disruptive to SLAs.
- Grace: pull customer-facing latency-sensitive routes and mark which can tolerate batching window of up to 150ms.
- Elena: confirm whether FinTechCo reserved bursts we discussed last month are still available for Aug–Sep.

I want the runbook to include: hot/cold GPU pools, pre-warm/process reuse strategy, prefix/KV caching expectations, batching experiments with window/latency tradeoffs, and an escalation path if utilization causes SLA-risk. We're aiming for a 12–18% improvement to per-token infra cost from changes we can ship in 4–6 weeks. If any of you think that target is unrealistic, call it out and propose alternate numbers.

Next steps: please reply with updates by EOD Wed (Aug 11). We'll run a short 30m alignment on Thu (Aug 12) to lock the deck.

Thanks,

Lauren Bishop
VP, Infrastructure & Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: infra-qbr-runbook-v1.pdf (PDF, 1.8MB), qbr-slot-planning.xlsx (XLSX, 240KB)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena@cloudops.io>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR prep — slot/runbook review: GPU cost & utilization levers

Lauren — thanks, sending a quick sketch of levers I think are high-impact and low-risk. Adding numbers from last-week telemetry.

Summary (rough):
- Batching window tuning (150ms -> 300ms for non-interactive routes): ~12–18% per-token reduction; rollout 2–3 weeks with canary.
- Prefix/KV cache tuning (increase on-host KV capacity, 2x): ~6–9% reduction; needs kernel config and small model-variant rebuilds; 3–5 weeks.
- Hot-pool prewarm (reserve warm instances for peak pattern customers): reduces cold-start cost and token tail latency; net cost neutral if we reuse warm instances 60%+; operationalize via hot/cold split and warm recycling policy; 1–2 weeks to script.
- Quantized model variant for background jobs (8-bit): ~20–30% GPU-hour reduction but needs quality guardrails; 4–8 weeks for rollout and eval harness.

Telemetry snippets (last 7 days):
- Average GPU utilization (production pools): 55%
- 95th pct token latency on interactive routes: 210ms
- Avg batching window currently: 87ms

Immediate asks from infra:
1) Approval to run a 2-week batching window A/B on non-interactive routes (start Aug 13). Expected 18% token-cost drop for those routes with <2% customer-visible latency regressions.
2) Permission to provision a small hot-pool of 40 gpus for FinTechCo (to be reclaimed if unused). Will seek finance sign-off on the hold cost.

I attached a short spec for the batching experiment (batching-cache-expt-spec.md). If we go ahead, Aditya and I will coordinate runbook changes and a fallout fallback (automatic revert after 1% SLA error rate).

—Markus

--
Markus Klein
Director, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: batching-cache-expt-spec.md (TXT, 14KB)

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@cloudops.io>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR prep — slot/runbook review: GPU cost & utilization levers

Lauren/Markus — confirming FinTechCo reserved burst pool is still available for Aug–Sep under the provisional commitment we discussed. We can hold up to 50 GPU-equivalent slots (A100-eq) with a 14-day notice and a two-week grace on usage. I can share the commitment letter (DocuSign) if you want to lock it.

Notes:
- We can also add pre-warm hooks on our side (short pre-pull images) to reduce instance spin-up to ~30s from 90s for warm nodes.
- Pricing: reserved burst has a 12% discount vs on-demand for the short-term window.

Link to commitment draft: https://cloudops.io/commitments/fintechco-draft (internal).

—Elena

Elena Ruiz
Enterprise Partnerships
CloudOps.io

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR prep — slot/runbook review: GPU cost & utilization levers

Quick forecast update per Markus' asks. I pulled the week-on-week consumption and modeled three scenarios (conservative / baseline / aggressive).

Key numbers (baseline):
- Current avg GPU hours/wk: 12,800 GPU-hours
- Projected w/ batching + KV tuning (baseline): 10,520 GPU-hours (18% reduction)
- Projected spend delta (baseline): approx $210k/mo -> $172k/mo (savings $38k/mo)
- Target utilization after changes: 68% (from 55%)

Assumptions: batching only applied to ~42% of token volume (non-interactive jobs); KV cache improvements assume 30% more cache-hit ratio for repeated prefixes; quantized variant used for background ingestion only.

Operational asks:
- Greenlight for the 2-week batching A/B starting Aug 13. We'll run K6 load tests first in staging on Aug 11.
- OK to provision 40 hot-pool GPUs for FinTechCo while we measure (Elena to confirm billing terms).

I've opened JIRA INFRA-4123 to track canary and rollback steps. Also added a tab to the qbr-sheet with per-route cost impact.

-Aditya

--
Aditya Rao
Head of Serving Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Related: JIRA-INFRA-4123, https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-id/Infra-QBR-Runbook

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena@cloudops.io>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR prep — slot/runbook review: GPU cost & utilization levers

Thanks, all — this is actionable and within the time window we need. Quick confirmation and action items for the QBR deck and runbook: 

1) Approve batching A/B (2-week) — Approved. Markus/Aditya, start on Aug 13, canary to 5% of traffic; rollback threshold: 1% SLA error or >5% latency regressions on sampled routes.
2) Hot-pool reservation — Approved provisional hold for 40 GPUs; Elena please push the DocuSign and finance will sign.
3) Deck ask: Aditya, add a one-slide before/after with unit-econ delta (GPU-hours, $/k-token, utilization change) and a short sensitivity table for +/- 5% batching effectiveness.
4) Runbook: Markus/Grace to add an "operational play" section that includes immediate rollback steps and a single-command revert.

We'll review the runbook and the updated numbers in Thu's 30m sync (Aug 12, 10:00–10:30 PDT). If you don't have edits in Drive by EOD Wed, I'll assume the numbers above are the basis for the Executive QBR.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Lauren

Attachments referenced: none in this note.
